teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Identify the position of the median for $n = 15$.
$$\text{Position of median} = \frac{15 + 1}{2} = 8\text{th value}$$
Counting the 8th value in the ordered Rebels list:
$$\text{Median} = 84\text{ kg}$$

Step 2: Identify the quartiles.
- The lower half consists of the 7 values below the median: $75, 78, 79, 80, 82, 82, 83$.
  The lower quartile $Q_1$ is the middle of these 7 values (the 4th overall value):
  $$Q_1 = 80\text{ kg}$$
- The upper half consists of the 7 values above the median: $85, 86, 89, 93, 95, 99, 102$.
  The upper quartile $Q_3$ is the middle of these 7 values (the 12th overall value):
  $$Q_3 = 93\text{ kg}$$

Step 3: Calculate the interquartile range:
$$\operatorname{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1 = 93 - 80 = 13\text{ kg}$$

hints: Compare either a measure of central tendency (median) or a measure of spread (interquartile range or range).
The median weight of Rebels (84 kg) is higher than the median weight of Sharks (76 kg).

Alternatively, compare the spread: the range of weights of the Rebels (27 kg) is greater than that of the Sharks (26 kg), or the interquartile range of the Rebels (13 kg) is greater than that of the Sharks (11 kg).
Make sure to state your comparison in context by referring to the weights of the players.
walkthrough: Compare the medians in context: The median weight of the players in the Rebels club (84 kg) is greater than the median weight of the players in the Sharks club (76 kg), indicating that on average the Rebels players are heavier.

Alternatively, compare the spread in context: The interquartile range of the weights of the Rebels players (13 kg) is greater than the interquartile range of the Sharks players (11 kg), showing greater variation in the middle 50% of the Rebels weights.
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Choose a statistical measure to compare.
When comparing two distributions from box plots, examiners accept either:
- A comparison of central tendency (the median)
- A comparison of spread (the interquartile range or range)

Step 2: Formulate the contextual statement clearly.
- Comparison of average/median: 'The median weight of players in the Rebels is higher than the median weight of players in the Sharks.' (Or: 'On average, the Rebels players are heavier than the Sharks players.')
- Comparison of spread: 'The range of weights of the Rebels players (102 - 75 = 27 kg) is greater than the range of weights of the Sharks players (92 - 66 = 26 kg).'
Note: You must explicitly mention the context ('weights of the players') rather than making a generic statement like 'the Rebels are bigger'.
